headline: Committee defers energy contract item, takes up Bill 181 homeowner exemption increase

meeting.body: Maui County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee
meeting.summary: The chair postponed the Johnson Controls Inc. energy performance contract. On Bill 181 (2025), which would raise two property tax exemptions, the chair asked about deferring, and a motion to file and its second were withdrawn. No final action is stated.
meeting.recap: The committee took up the Johnson Controls Inc. energy performance contract.[[0:08:35]] The administration said Phase 1 of the energy project is done and is saving money.[[0:10:40]] The committee was told the project cost about $25 million, with net savings of $11.9 million.[[0:33:04]] The next phase would cost a little over $9 million, paid back each year for 20 years at 4.4%.[[0:34:17]] The chair deferred (postponed) the item.[[0:45:00]] The committee took up Bill 181 (2025), which would raise the homeowner exemption from $300,000 to $400,000 and the long-term rental exemption from $200,000 to $300,000.[[0:51:12]] A testifier said the increase would give the biggest benefit to the highest-value homes.[[0:55:53]] The finance director said the change would cost $4.9 million for homeowners and $1.4 million for long-term rentals.[[1:05:50]] The finance director said rates and tiers give the council more flexibility than exemptions.[[1:07:37]] A council member moved to file the bill, and another member seconded.[[1:28:17]] The motion and the second were withdrawn.[[1:36:21]]
meeting.next: The administration said it will give the council the energy savings audit results when it gets them.

moments.q: Project cost and net savings explained
"You're giving the greatest benefit to the people with the highest value homes."

issues.oneLine: Bill 181 would raise the homeowner property tax exemption to $400,000 and the long-term rental exemption to $300,000.
issues.why: A council member said the bill gives $6.3 million in tax relief and wants it to go to people who need it most.

deadlines.t: When a homeowner exemption change would start to affect people.

issues.next: The chair asked if members were open to deferring the bill and taking it up again.
issues.brief: The Department of Finance estimated the homeowner part would cut property tax revenue by $4,919,184 and affect 25,063 parcels.[[#1]] A testifier said about 3,000 homeowners who pay minimum tax would get no help from the increase.[[#2]]
